title: PolarisDesktopOperationPrimitives
description: Desktop operation vocabulary: the closed Phase-01 and Phase-02 operation subsets, their effect classification, their caller class and their trust boundary. Shared by the envelope binding, the IPC registries and the error mapping.
$comment: مفردات عمليات سطح المكتب. المجموعة الفرعية مغلقة كما الأصل مغلق: عملية خارجها غير قابلة للتمثيل لا مرفوضة وقت التشغيل فقط.

Phase01DesktopOperation.title: Phase01DesktopOperation
Phase01DesktopOperation.description: The five read-only desktop operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.1 (ADR-017). This is a strict subset of IPCEnvelopeV1 Operation; a parity test proves the two never drift.

Phase02DesktopOperation.title: Phase02DesktopOperation
Phase02DesktopOperation.description: The nineteen Phase-02 operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.2 (ADR-019). A strict subset of IPCEnvelopeV1 Operation; a parity test proves the two never drift.

OperationEffect.title: OperationEffect
OperationEffect.description: Effect classification. Every Phase-01 desktop operation is READ_ONLY. A SIDE_EFFECTING operation enters the idempotency conditional of the envelope in the same change.

IdempotencyRequirement.title: IdempotencyRequirement
IdempotencyRequirement.description: Whether the envelope must carry idempotency_key. READ_ONLY implies NOT_REQUIRED; the registry test proves the implication holds.

TrustBoundary.title: TrustBoundary
TrustBoundary.description: The boundary an operation crosses. Phase-01 has exactly one; naming it makes a second one a visible contract change rather than an accident.

CallerClass.title: CallerClass
CallerClass.description: Which class of caller may issue the operation. This is the class the native gateway stamps, never a value the renderer asserts. It maps onto the frozen CallerType CORE_UI at the envelope level; the registry names the class, the envelope names the type.

CallerIdentityAuthority.title: CallerIdentityAuthority
CallerIdentityAuthority.description: Who decides caller identity for the operation. NATIVE_TRANSPORT means the host stamps identity from the transport and overwrites whatever the renderer asserted.

OwningService.title: OwningService
OwningService.description: The single native service that answers the operation. One owner per operation; there is no dispatcher service.

SchemaReference.title: SchemaReference
SchemaReference.description: A schema file path relative to contracts/schemas, plus a JSON Pointer to the definition inside it. The registry consistency test resolves every reference against the loaded schema set, so a dangling reference fails the build.

EffectClass.title: EffectClass
EffectClass.description: Phase-02 effect class. READ has no side effect; READ_RESOURCE reads a user-authorised local resource; WRITE_CONFIG and SECRET_WRITE change trusted settings or the credential store; CREATE_LOCAL_DATA and WRITE_LOCAL_DATA change the product database; NETWORK_PROBE contacts a provider endpoint; MODEL_INVOCATION sends a request to a model provider; CONTROL changes the state of an in-flight operation. A side effect is never hidden under READ.

Phase03DesktopOperation.title: Phase03DesktopOperation
Phase03DesktopOperation.description: The ten Phase-03 operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.3. There is no agent.execute, agent.call or orchestrator.command: an operation whose payload could name an arbitrary action is not in this set and cannot be added to it without changing this contract.

Phase04DesktopOperation.title: Phase04DesktopOperation
Phase04DesktopOperation.description: The twelve Phase-04 operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.4. There is no tool.execute, tool.invoke or mcp.call: the renderer can read the registry and answer an approval, and nothing here can run a tool. Tool invocation has exactly one caller, the trusted mission runtime, and exactly one path, the tool gateway.

Phase05DesktopOperation.title: Phase05DesktopOperation
Phase05DesktopOperation.description: The twelve Phase-05 operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.5. There is no browser.raw_execute, computer.raw_command or memory.trust: the renderer can read sessions and memory, delete a memory, grant a window to a mission and stop a session, and nothing here can navigate, click, type or raise the trust of a memory. Browser and computer actions have exactly one caller, the trusted mission runtime, and exactly one path, the tool gateway.

Phase06DesktopOperation.title: Phase06DesktopOperation
Phase06DesktopOperation.description: The twenty-eight Phase-06 operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.6. There is no connector.invoke, connector.execute or connector.call: the renderer registers, configures, tests and reads connectors, budgets, prices, observability and settings, and nothing here performs a connector operation on a service. Connector operations have exactly one caller, the trusted mission runtime, and exactly one path, the tool gateway and then the connector gateway. No operation reveals a credential value.

Phase08DesktopOperation.title: Phase08DesktopOperation
Phase08DesktopOperation.description: The forty-three Phase-08 operations added by IPCEnvelopeV1 1.7 (the four conversation.* members later, ADR-029; agent.catalog and mission.specialist.set later still, ADR-030; conversation.update, conversation.delete and project.delete after them, ADR-031; memory.remember, ADR-032; conversation.search, ADR-031). There is no execution.command, execution.python, workspace.write, browser.execute, oauth.token.get or email.send: the renderer attaches files, reads workspaces, artifacts and runs, edits schedules, connections, grants and settings, and decides what waits for its decision. Commands, Python, browsing and workspace writes have exactly one caller, the trusted mission runtime, and exactly one path, the tool gateway. The ten web.search.*, mission.rating.set, mission.note.add, tool.approval.grants, tool.approval.grant.revoke and github.* members were added additively at 1.7 later still (ADR-042).
